guidance.heading: Third Quarter Fiscal Year 2027 Outlook
section: The following statements are based on current expectations. These statements are forward-looking, and actual results may differ materially.

Net Sales | $1.573 to $1.638 billion
GAAP(5) | Non-GAAP Adjustments(1) | Non-GAAP(1)
Gross Profit | 62.9% to 63.9% | $17.7 to $18.7 million | 64.0% to 65.0%
Operating Expenses(2) | 36.7% to 37.4% | $163.0 to $167.0 million | 26.5% to 27.0%
Operating Income | 25.5% to 27.2% | $180.8 to $185.8 million | 37.0% to 38.5%
Other Expense, net | $47.7 to $48.3 million | $(0.2) to $0.2 million | $47.5 to $48.5 million
Income Tax Provision | $67.1 to $91.3 million(3) | $(53.4) to $(32.4) million | $34.7 to $37.9 million(4)
Net income | $285.9 to $305.8 million | $212.9 to $239.3 million | $498.8 to $545.1 million
Dividends on Series A Preferred Stock | $(27.8) million | $27.8 million | —
Net income attributable to common stockholders | $258.1 to $278.0 million | $240.7 to $267.1 million | $498.8 to $545.1 million
Diluted Common Shares Outstanding | Approximately 551.0 to 552.0 million shares | 23.8 million shares | Approximately 574.8 to 575.8 million shares
Diluted net income per common share | $0.47 to $0.50 | $0.40 to $0.45 | $0.87 to $0.95
(1) See the "Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures" section of this release for information regarding our non-GAAP guidance.

(2) We are not able to estimate the amount of certain Special Charges and Other, net that may be incurred during the quarter ending December 31, 2026. Therefore, our estimate of GAAP operating expenses excludes certain amounts that may be recognized as Special Charges and Other, net in the quarter ending December 31, 2026.
(3) The forecast for GAAP tax expense excludes any unexpected tax events that may occur during the quarter, as these amounts cannot be forecasted.
(4) Represents the expected cash tax rate for fiscal 2027, excluding any transition tax payments associated with the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act.

(5) Our GAAP guidance excludes the impact of any potential gains or charges related to our ongoing evaluation of restructuring activities including the sale of our Fab 2 wafer fabrication facility in Tempe, Arizona.

Capital expenditures for the quarter ending December 31, 2026 are expected to be about $35 million. Capital expenditures for all of fiscal 2027 are expected to be approximately $100 million. Consistent with the slow macroeconomic environment in fiscal 2025, we have paused most of our factory expansion actions and reduced our planned capital investments through fiscal 2027. However, we are adding capital equipment to selectively expand our production capacity and add research and development equipment.

desk.headline: Sales up 42% to $1.62bn, above the top of its own range and a beat; December-quarter outlook below estimates as supply tightens
results: Net sales rose 42.2% from a year ago and 9.2% from the June quarter to $1.62bn, beating the $1.604bn midpoint it guided in August.
Adjusted EPS was $0.97 (guide was $0.91–0.95), up from $0.35; GAAP EPS jumped to $0.68 from $0.03.
Non-GAAP gross margin climbed to 66.5% from 56.7%, while operating costs grew much more slowly than sales.
Free cash flow was $396.1m; about $247.6m went to shareholders as dividends, and cash rose to $457m.
Bought edge-AI chip firm Hailo (September) and space-grade chip maker Vorago (October).

guidance.summary: For the December quarter Microchip expects sales of $1.573–1.638bn (down 3% to up 1% from September) and adjusted EPS of $0.87–0.95. It says this is better than normal seasonality once about $53m of one-off September sales is excluded; call coverage said the sales range fell short of analyst estimates.

points: Supply, not demand, is now the limit: lead times have stretched to roughly 6–32 weeks as foundry and test capacity is absorbed by data-centre chips.
Data-centre sales topped $250m in the quarter; CEO Steve Sanghi still described data centre as being "in the bubble" while calling other demand normal.
Bookings stayed strong with book-to-bill well above one; PCIe Gen6 switch and retimer design wins doubled to 24.
Margin hopes were reset: about 65% gross margin is now framed as a target rather than a floor, and supplier price rises from January will be absorbed.
Inventory days rose to 184 from 175; extra outsourced test capacity is planned from the March quarter.
call.source: Press release outlook; call coverage: Earnings Whispers via Finviz, 5 Nov 2026, and Tech Insider, 7 Nov 2026

watch: Whether added wafer and test capacity lets sales outrun the December guide.
Gross margin holding near 64–65% as supplier price rises land from January.
Data-centre sales pace and the build-up in inventory days.
